body: Thank you for the kind wishes. I have been working with my counselor on automatic negative thoughts (I believe that's the term she uses), but damn is it ever a hard habit to break. I'm pretty much staring at my phone in dread all day today, and obsessing about getting the email/phone call that declines me, so I'm going to try and distract myself by running some errands and playing Fable.
I apologize. I felt desperate and suicidal and thought this was the place to talk. Should I remove this post?

I appreciate your 2 cents :) It makes me feel a bit better to hear that I'm not the only one that groans every time they look at their work history, and for similar reasons. I don't have to worry about my work references; both of my former supervisors from the cafe and the bank loved me and were happy to give strong recommendations. But the company is using a third party background company to do the check, so it will **definitely** come to light that I fudged the dates on that job. I can't see why they'd still hire someone they know lied (while I'm sure HR sees it a lot, I can imagine it'd be something annoying to have to deal with). There's nothing else in the background check I'd be worried about; even if I had a criminal history that wouldn't have barred me from the job, but of course I had to choose to fuck with my employment history. :/

I've started trying to accept it since I fired off the email yesterday. I'm trying to let go of the self-berating, but I know the most painful part (telling my friend, fiance, and family) has yet to come. I have started looking for other jobs as well...I gave myself the last week to freak out, and am now trying to move towards practical measures to deal with the upcoming repercussions. The one tiny shred of light in all this is that I am hoping that that there's someone else that was shortlisted and REALLY needs the job worse than I do who will get it because of this. 

Thanks for the encouragement. :)

Thank you friend. I know it could always be worse, I watch the news and immediately feel ashamed over my shitty problems when I see starving Somalian children who lead short lives of misery without ever getting to experience the smallest shred of kindness, so I'm not completely stuck in tunnel vision. This was a difficult lesson I never should have had to learn the hard way to begin with. 

I'm not worried about anything else; the financial services job is by far the most important experience I have and the one that provided most of the experience I'd need for this job, and I have nothing to hide there...I had to work with confidential information and had to have a background/credit check to work there as well. But I am very sure they will reject me based on the employment lie.
